title: GTM Canonicals — Vertical Entry
$comment: Schema scope — the top-level shape describes a VERTICAL entry; #/definitions/manifest describes _manifest.yaml; #/definitions/campaign_manifest (BC-11852, schema v2) describes docs/campaigns/<entity>/<slug>/manifest.json. Editor tooling (e.g., yaml-language-server) MUST NOT validate _manifest.yaml against the top-level vertical shape; reference #/definitions/manifest explicitly via a yaml-language-server directive at the top of _manifest.yaml when IDE support is added.
description: Thin schema per ADR-016 (D7). One file per vertical under plugins/marketing/data/canonicals/{slug}.yaml. _manifest.yaml shape is documented in #/definitions/manifest (schema_version: 2 since BC-11852 to admit the audience_tiers block). Campaign manifests (docs/campaigns/<entity>/<slug>/manifest.json) are described in #/definitions/campaign_manifest (schema_version: 2 since BC-11852). Brite repo is stdlib-only — this schema is the declarative contract; plugins/marketing/scripts/lint_canonicals.py is the runtime enforcement (it mirrors the constraints below).

slug.description: Strict kebab-case canonical slug. Matches filename ({slug}.yaml). No trailing or doubled hyphens.

aliases.description: Optional. Kebab-case slugs that should resolve to this vertical (for renames). Must not collide with any canonical vertical slug or another vertical's alias.

playbook_path.description: Optional. Path to handbook playbook README, relative to handbook root.

personas.description: May be empty for skeleton entries (per D11).

offers.description: May be empty for skeleton entries (per D11).

titles.description: >=1 required (drives list-building title cascade per ADR-016).

target_personas.description: Each entry must resolve to a persona.slug in the same vertical (enforced by lint_canonicals.py).

target_postures.description: Optional advisory per ADR-017 §57-62. Each campaign-instance posture may override.

replaced_by.description: Forward-pointer to the offer slug that supersedes this one (must reference a sibling offer.slug in the same vertical).

iterates_from.description: Reverse-pointer to the offer slug this one iterates on (must reference a sibling offer.slug in the same vertical).

prose_path.description: Optional. Path to handbook offer prose, relative to handbook root.

manifest.$comment: Shape of _manifest.yaml. Enforced by plugins/marketing/scripts/lint_canonicals.py (Brite repo has no jsonschema runtime dependency). schema_version bumped 1 → 2 in BC-11852 to admit the audience_tiers block.

schema_version.description: Pinned to the linter's SCHEMA_VERSION constant. Bumped 1 → 2 in BC-11852 (introduces the audience_tiers block).

verticals.description: Alphabetized + duplicate-free list of canonical vertical slugs (>=1 required).

audience_tiers.description: BC-11852: canonical audience-tier slugs + display + observed EB-name matches. Empirically derived from docs/reconciliation/master-index.json (PR #391). The auto-classifier (BC-11849 import-campaign) maps EB campaign-name strings to a structured audience_tier object via the 'matches' substrings here. See ADR-020.

audience_tier_entry.$comment: Per-axis entry inside audience_tiers[] in _manifest.yaml. The audience-tier taxonomy decomposes into THREE orthogonal axes (per ADR-020): 'tier' (ESP/email-type), 'seniority' (job-level filter), and 'modifiers' (orthogonal copy/data flags). Each entry below names one slug on one axis. The 'matches' field is a list of substring tokens that, when found in an EB campaign name, indicate this slug applies — a single EB name maps to ONE tier slug + AT MOST ONE seniority slug + ZERO OR MORE modifier slugs.

slug.description: Strict kebab-case canonical slug for this axis-value.

axis.description: Which axis this slug belongs to. 'tier' = ESP/email-type (e.g., professional, role); 'seniority' = job-level filter (e.g., managers-plus, employees); 'modifier' = orthogonal flag (e.g., reverified, direct-question-offer).

description.description: Optional. One-line explanation of what this slug means semantically.

matches.description: Optional. Substring tokens that, when present in an EB campaign name, indicate this slug applies. Used by the BC-11849 import-campaign auto-classifier. Case-insensitive match — the classifier lowercases both sides. Empty/omitted means manual classification only.

campaign_manifest.$comment: Shape of docs/campaigns/<entity>/<slug>/manifest.json. Schema v2 introduced in BC-11852 — email_bison.campaign_id (singular) replaced by email_bison.campaigns[] (one entry per EB campaign record across ESPs + audience_tiers, since a single logical Brite campaign may produce multiple EB records — empirically up to 6 per docs/reconciliation/master-index.md). email_bison.workspace is retained as the primary-workspace pointer (where the canonical lead list lives), distinct from campaigns[].workspace which records the workspace each EB record was created in.

schema_version.description: v2 per BC-11852. v1 manifests must be migrated via plugins/marketing/scripts/migrate_manifest_v1_to_v2.py before they will validate.

vertical.description: Vertical slug — must resolve to a canonical vertical in plugins/marketing/data/canonicals/_manifest.yaml verticals[].

offer_posture.description: Optional override of the offer-canonical posture for this campaign instance per ADR-017.

created_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at scaffold time.

segments.description: Optional (ADR-024). Discovery-ICP segment names chosen at scaffold time — each must resolve to a segment key in plugins/marketing/data/canonicals/icp/{vertical}.json. Per-segment criteria copies live at docs/campaigns/{entity}/tam/{slug}/{segment}/icp.json.

email_bison_block_v2.$comment: v2 email_bison block. workspace = PRIMARY-workspace pointer (where the canonical lead list lives — distinct from each EB record's workspace in campaigns[].workspace). campaign_id (singular) is INTENTIONALLY REMOVED — replaced by campaigns[] array. campaign_name retained for cross-walks against Salesforce.campaign_name and EB-name auto-classify.

workspace.description: Primary workspace — where the canonical lead list is imported. The two Brite EB workspaces are b2b (professional/role audience) and personal (personal-email audience).

campaign_name.description: Logical campaign name (typically matches slug). Used for cross-walks against Salesforce.campaign_name and as the auto-classifier seed for EB record naming.

campaigns.description: EB campaign records — one entry per (workspace × audience_tier × ESP) split. Empty array = not yet launched. A single logical Brite campaign may produce multiple EB records (empirically up to 6, e.g., Professional Emails + Personal Emails + Role Emails across both workspaces).

workspace.description: EB workspace this record was created in.

campaign_id.description: EB campaign ID (numeric). String form admitted because earlier EB MCP responses serialized as string; both shapes are accepted on read.

esp.description: Email Service Provider this record targets (e.g., 'gmail-workspace', 'office365', 'all'). Free-form — EB does not enforce an ESP enum.

name.description: EB-side campaign name (as it appears in EB UI). May include composite suffixes like '| Professional Emails | All ESPs'.

launched_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp when this EB record was launched. Null until launched.

status.description: EB-side status. Defaults to 'draft' on creation; transitions through launched/paused/completed/archived.

pending_classification.description: Set true by migrate_manifest_v1_to_v2.py when a v1 launched-but-unclassified campaign is auto-migrated with a placeholder audience_tier. Operators clear this flag once they've classified the record via /marketing:import-campaign (BC-11849).

discovery_icp.$comment: Shape of plugins/marketing/data/canonicals/icp/{vertical}.json per ADR-024. One file per registered vertical — presence is ERROR-enforced by lint_canonicals.py. Segments-only: no base block; a single-audience vertical is the one-segment case. Stub form: segments empty REQUIRES clarifications_needed non-empty (lint-enforced). The contact half (personas + titles) stays in the sibling {vertical}.yaml; this file is the discovery half (which companies are in this market).

vertical.description: Must match the filename ({vertical}.json) and resolve to a canonical vertical slug in _manifest.yaml verticals[].

source.description: Pointer to the prose source material — handbook vertical README path, or references/vertical-playbooks/{vertical}.md for the 6 playbook verticals.

clarifications_needed.description: Operator-fill items. MUST be non-empty when segments is empty (stub form). May remain non-empty on a ready file to flag unresolved caveats.

segments.description: Named account universes. Each segment is a SELF-CONTAINED Discovery ICP — never a sparse override; no merge semantics (ADR-024).

icp_segment.$comment: One account universe inside a discovery_icp. Core keys mirror references/tam/icp-definition.md verbatim so the flattened campaign copy parses in the tam-map/*_client.py scripts unchanged; display/persona/seed_accounts are additive (clients access keys by name and ignore extras).

persona.description: Cross-reference to the contact cascade that pairs with this account universe — must resolve to a persona.slug in the sibling {vertical}.yaml (enforced by lint_canonicals.py).

size_band.description: Null where the floor/ceiling is genuinely open. Proxy semantics (e.g., sq-ft GLA expressed via notes in intent_signals) belong in the authored values, not new keys.

seed_accounts.description: Durable look-alike exemplars for this universe (ADR-024: vertical-level market knowledge; campaign copies may prune/extend). Optional — some universes are definable purely by criteria.

domain.description: Optional at authoring time; what look-alike tooling keys on.

audience_tier_object.$comment: Structured audience-tier per ADR-020. Three orthogonal axes — tier (REQUIRED), seniority (optional), modifiers (optional list). Slug values are validated against the _manifest.yaml audience_tiers[] block at lint time.

tier.description: Primary ESP/email-type axis (e.g., professional, role, personal, general).

seniority.description: Optional job-level filter (e.g., managers-plus, employees, bar-owners-gms). Null when not specified.

modifiers.description: Optional orthogonal flags (e.g., reverified, direct-question-offer). Empty array when none apply.
